newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, then jumps on AGA data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, then jumps on AGA data.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, pressured by profit taking after recent gains, ended down Wednesday in a moderate session, then gained in after-hours trade following bullish weekly inventory data, sources said.

September slipped 2.3 cents to close at $2.351 per million British thermal units, then jumped to $2.42 on ACCESS after the AGA report. October settled 2.5 cents lower at $2.356, while other deferreds ended down by 0.4 to 3.5 cents.

"It (the AGA number) was well below estimates. It should be a catalyst for continued strength in the Gulf. Baseload deals in the Gulf are getting done at index plus 20 cents which is a huge number," said Chris Bray at United Fuels, who had expected a build in the 55 to 70 bcf range.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 55 bcf, well-below average estimates in the 70-75 bcf range.
Overall inventories now are just 133 bcf, or 7.5 percent, above last year's record lows and still lag the three-year average by more than 10 percent.

Eastern inventories increased by 50 bcf last week and remained 28 bcf, or three percent, over last year. Consuming region west storage, which gained seven bcf last week, continued to lag 1996 levels by about one percent. Stocks in the producing region, which fell two bcf for the week, were still 28 percent above last year.

Despite extended forecasts calling for mostly normal to below-normal temperatures for the eastern half of the nation, some said continued heat out West and decent injection demand may be enough to underpin physical prices near-term.
But many remain skeptical current levels can be sustained without a broader heat wave to stir better cooling demand.

Chart traders pegged September resistance at the new contract high of $2.43, whick also coincides with the May 7 spot continuation high, and then in the $2.48 area. Minor support was seen at $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.20, then at $2.15-2.16 and along the short-term up trendline at $2.13.

In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed almost five cents to the mid-$2.30s. Midcon pipes were up a few cents to near the $2.30 level. New York city gate prices held relatively steady in the low-$2.50s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip fell 2.5 cents to $2.309. NYMEX said 41,066 contracts traded, down sharply from Tuesday's revised tally of 71,663.
On the KCBT, September finished 1.5 cents higher at $2.265, while deferreds ended steady to down one cent. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.8 cents to 8.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
